roots.note: common FoLang source parser root for package files, src/appl.fol, src/component.fol, and every components/<kind>/component.fol surface, including operators

UnsupportedFeature.meaning: recognized feature or reserved future form is unsupported by the active language profile

UnsupportedBackendFeature.meaning: required representation or facility is unsupported by the selected backend contract

InvalidIdentifier.meaning: identifier violates spelling, underscore, reserved-word, or encoding rules

InvalidLiteral.meaning: literal violates its normative lexical or structural form

UnexpectedToken.meaning: token cannot occur at the current grammar position

ExpectedToken.meaning: required delimiter, binder, separator, operand, or token is absent

InvalidSyntax.meaning: source violates a grammar rule without a more specific registered parser diagnostic

UnknownOperator.meaning: complete symbolic run is neither built in nor registered in the active operator table

InvalidProjectLayout.meaning: project root, component tree, fixed surface, filename role, or project-kind layout is invalid

InvalidSourcePlacement.meaning: file, declaration, unit, block form, directive, pragma, or component surface appears in a forbidden source context

InvalidDeclarationForm.meaning: declaration has an unsupported head, nesting, body, filename-derived name, classifier combination, or structural shape

ReservedPackageShadowing.meaning: project or dependency content attempts to shadow the installed co.* package identity

InvalidImport.meaning: import has an invalid form, target, alias, visibility, role, or source context

InvalidDependency.meaning: dependency crosses a forbidden project, component, capability, or packaged-library direction

CapabilityViolation.meaning: source accesses or enables a facility outside its permitted capability domain

ExportBoundaryViolation.meaning: public, projected, or packaged surface exposes a forbidden or inaccessible representation

DuplicateDeclaration.meaning: non-callable declarations normalize to one symbol in the same namespace

DuplicateCallableSignature.meaning: callables normalize to the same owner, receiver category, name, and parameter signature

AmbiguousSymbol.meaning: more than one symbol remains after applicable qualification and resolution

InaccessibleSymbol.meaning: resolved declaration is not accessible from the requesting context

InvalidReceiver.meaning: receiver is absent, has the wrong category, or does not match its required owner

UnusedImport.meaning: import contributes no live resolved use under strict import-liveness rules

UnusedSymbol.meaning: declaration subject to strict liveness is not reachable or used as required

TypeMismatch.meaning: actual and required canonical types or callable shapes are incompatible

ConstraintViolation.meaning: value or type violates a refinement, relation set, bound, variance, capability, or declared constraint

InvalidAssignment.meaning: assignment target, source, binding operator, mutability rule, or transfer relationship is invalid

Uninitialized.meaning: a refinement/dependent value is read where valid assignment is not proven on every reachable path

InvalidNoneUse.meaning: none, isNone(), or missing-result none substitution is used with a non-none refinement/dependent position

InvalidDependentIndex.meaning: dependent index has an invalid form, resolution, evaluability, sign, or source

DependentTypeMismatch.meaning: dependent constructors or normalized indices do not match where equality is required

InvalidConstruction.meaning: construction or initialization path cannot produce a valid readable value

MutationNotAllowed.meaning: source attempts a statically detectable mutation through a non-mutable root

OverloadNotAllowed.meaning: declaration category or callable identity cannot introduce the requested overload

NoApplicableOverload.meaning: no visible overload accepts the resolved receiver and argument types

AmbiguousOverload.meaning: multiple incomparable most-specific overload candidates remain applicable

InvalidReturn.meaning: return binding, count, type, named-result use, or required result production is invalid

MissingImplementation.meaning: required body, interface method, abstract or virtual slot, runtime binding, or implementation is absent

InvalidForwardDeclaration.meaning: bodyless declaration has invalid classification, mapping, signature, or forward metadata

InvalidGenericDeclaration.meaning: generic marker, rank, placement, declaration head, classifier combination, or parameter structure is invalid

InvalidGenericMapping.meaning: generic mapping is conflicting, cyclic, structurally incompatible, absent where required, or incomplete

GenericResolutionFailure.meaning: generic arguments or result markers cannot resolve to one consistent permitted assignment

SignatureConformanceFailure.meaning: declaration fails its required structural signature

InvalidAssociatedTypeBinding.meaning: associated-type binding is missing, unknown, incompatible, or violates declared generic requirements

InvalidRelationship.meaning: interface, class, mixin, or trait relationship has an invalid kind, target, count, selector, accessibility, or identity

InheritedMemberConflict.meaning: inherited state or behavior conflicts and cannot be resolved automatically

InvalidOverride.meaning: override target, source category, accessibility, sealing rule, or signature is invalid

InvalidImplementation.meaning: explicit implementation mapping selects an invalid source, target, method, accessibility, or signature

InvalidLifecycleDeclaration.meaning: lifecycle declaration, invocation, metadata, placement, accessibility, or overload/override use is invalid

InvalidMemberPolicy.meaning: field or member carries a forbidden storage, mutability, sharing, locking, CopyOnWrite, static, or class policy

UnresolvedMetadataForm.meaning: user-defined annotation or decorator name cannot resolve to a valid metadata declaration

InvalidMetadataPlacement.meaning: metadata appears in a source location where its category is forbidden

InvalidMetadataTarget.meaning: resolved metadata form does not permit the attached declaration or expression kind

MissingMetadataField.meaning: required field of a recognized metadata form is absent

InvalidMetadataField.meaning: metadata field is unknown, duplicated, incorrectly bound, or forbidden for the selected context

InvalidMetadataValue.meaning: metadata value has an invalid type, cardinality, range, enumeration, declaration category, or compile-time status

ConflictingMetadata.meaning: individually valid metadata forms cannot govern or classify the same declaration together

InvalidOperatorDeclaration.meaning: custom operator declaration has invalid spelling, fixity, precedence, associativity, arity, attributes, ownership, or placement

InvalidOperatorOverload.meaning: operator implementation violates operand ownership, receiver, signature, arity/fixity, genericity, accessibility, or identity rules

InvalidEffectDeclaration.meaning: effects metadata, emitted error type, or declaration placement is invalid

InvalidEffectPolicy.meaning: call-site onEffect record has an invalid key, structure, placement, or context-specific policy shape

InvalidEffectHandler.meaning: handler list or handler module violates accessibility, uniqueness, module, signature, or nested-handling rules

InvalidEffectResolution.meaning: effect resolution is missing, duplicated, unknown, contextually forbidden, or result-incompatible

InvalidRetryPolicy.meaning: retry configuration has an invalid attempt count, exhaustion action, placement, or structure

InvalidExecutionModel.meaning: execution-model declaration or invocation violates result, effects, submission, boundary, or call-site handling rules

reference_consistency_warnings.detail: The Built-in Directives table note mentions @co.dap.overload while the predefined ANNOTATION registry contains no co.dap.overload entry. Under the strict built-in registry rule, @co.dap.overload is therefore not a recognized built-in metadata form unless the reference explicitly adds it.

The forall sections define forall as a contextual polymorphic type-expression binder, while the Rank-2 return examples still use forall-prefixed anonymous function-literal forms. The grammar retains the existing contextual anonymous-function/type form; the reference should keep the type-expression versus value-expression boundary explicit.

reference_consistency_warnings.status: semantic rule present; concrete source attachment syntax still unspecified
reference_consistency_warnings.detail: The reference defines class-inheritance-only augmentation of an inherited generic method's mapping set but does not yet define a concrete source form that attaches those mapping rows to the inherited method. No new grammar production is invented here.

The predicate-type example establishes the intended named-binder form. The reference should still state normatively that the binder is immutable, scoped only to the predicate body, denotes a co.lang.type candidate, and requires the body to resolve to co.lang.bool.
The reference identifies <: as subtype and :> as supertype but does not yet state whether those relations are proper or inclusive of canonical type equality.
The predicate-type example uses candidate.implements(...) and candidate.isAbstract, but their signatures and behavior are not yet defined as members of the co.lang.type descriptor API.

notes: Appendix C remains removed from the language reference; unique lexical/parser policy is carried by the normative sections and this standalone consolidated EBNF.

The built-in @co.* metadata registry in this grammar matches the latest reference inventory, including co.dap.implement, co.dap.implementation, co.dap.symbol, co.dap.effects, co.dap.onEffect, and co.dap.defer; recognized form names remain closed while fields of a recognized form are generically collected and preserved.

All project-local component surfaces use _ co.lang.component. application/native/dynamicvmrt are projected component kinds; packaged uses the export selector; operators contains co.lang.operator declarations only. Filesystem role supplies the component kind and structural validation context.
components/operators/component.fol uses the common component-surface-file parser root. There is no separate operator-source-file parser root in the consolidated grammar.
co.lang.extension has an active declaration production with mandatory ->(fortype=Type) targeting. It adds behavior without creating a subtype or changing the target inheritance hierarchy.

Function-shaped declarations are AST-classified by @co.dap.generic, @co.dap.decorator, @co.dap.extension, @co.dap.macro, @co.dap.template, @co.dap.native, @co.dap.executionmodel, @co.dap.operator, and @co.dap.indexer; all other function-shaped declarations remain FunctionDecl regardless of other non-classifying metadata.

Function-shape classifiers are mutually exclusive except for @co.dap.operator + @co.dap.extension. That deliberate composition remains one OperatorOverloadDecl; @co.dap.extension supplies the existing target/owner.
@co.dap.operator and @co.dap.generic are incompatible on the same declaration, with or without @co.dap.extension. Operators never introduce operator-level generic parameters.

A generic class, struct, or extension target may own or receive an operator, but operator ownership is associated with the generic type's canonical declaration identity. Owner type arguments do not become operator parameters and do not trigger generic-operator inference.
This operator/generic/extension clarification changes semantic validation and the zero-width function-shaped classification guard; it does not add a new lexical token or EBNF production.
Predicate types use a dedicated co.lang.type.where(identifier => expression) binder production; this does not enable general identifier => expression lambdas.
The type-relation operators <: and :> are active relational expressions at precedence 350 and use the common multi-symbol infix boundary guard.
Relational and equality grammar levels now admit at most one operator each, matching the reference's non-associative parse table.
A shared declarative-attribute-binder production requires '=' for named directive, annotation, pragma, and decorator fields recursively and for every co.lang.operator declaration attribute.
A balanced audit of all 235 @co.* metadata applications with argument lists in the language reference found zero colon binders.

The operator attributes fixity, precedence, associativity, arity, commutative, idempotent, identity, foldable, vectorizable, distributes_over, and desugar reject ':' as a binder. ':' remains valid for ordinary object fields and runtime map entries.

this is the single receiver keyword. It denotes the current instance in instance methods, the current class/type in class methods and @@new, the current instance in @@init, the fortype receiver in target-bound extensions, and the current singleton in object functions; static methods have no implicit receiver.

co.dap.effects is definer-owned callable metadata advertising an open, non-exhaustive set of known possible effects. Its absence does not make a callable effect-free, and undeclared effects may propagate.

The compiler computes known outgoing effects from explicit declarations plus known unhandled callee effects and the possibility of co.lang.GenericError from concrete handlers with known outgoing effects, minus consumed effects, and serializes that known set in .folenc metadata.
co.dap.onEffect is caller-owned expression metadata parsed only immediately before one call and rejected on callable definitions; its effect keys need not already be advertised by the callee.

For ordinary calls, onEffect uses direct effect-type fields, an optional non-empty handlers=[...] list, and exactly one singular resolution=continue|retry|return|return_with_error|propagate; unmatched effects propagate by default.

For execution-model calls, every onEffect entry requires handlers, forbids an explicit resolution, and uses the language-fixed implicit return_with_error policy; unmatched effects are converted without handlers.

retry reinvokes only the decorated call, evaluates receiver and argument expressions once, runs handlers for each failed attempt, and requires retry={max_attempts=PositiveCompileTimeInteger, on_exhausted=continue|return|return_with_error|propagate}.

co.core.EffectHandler is structural only. Each concrete handle implementation may independently advertise effects, but co.dap.onEffect is forbidden throughout every handler module so a handler cannot start a nested local handling pipeline.

When handlers are present, the same co.lang.error is passed synchronously to each caller-owned co.core.EffectHandler module in declared order before the resolution. Ordinary handlers run in the receiving caller context; execution-model handlers run in the effect-observation context before completion publication. There is no effects wrapper, resolutions list, or invoke resolution.

If handler H emits recoverable effect E1 while processing original effect E0, remaining handlers are skipped and E0's resolution is cancelled. The standard library creates co.lang.GenericError(E0,E1,H) with available causal, source, and runtime diagnostic context; the same handler list never processes that wrapper.

An ordinary handler failure propagates its co.lang.GenericError from the enclosing caller. An execution-model handler failure returns that wrapper through the ordinary error-result position and supplies co.const.none only to otherwise unproduced none-admitting results.

co.lang.GenericError is not used for normal propagate, return_with_error, or execution-model conversion; those preserve the original error object. Fatal handler failures terminate immediately and are never wrapped.

Ordinary uninitialized typed storage begins in the universal co.const.none state. None is not a singleton and has no stable observable identity; only intrinsic isNone() reliably observes it on types that admit none.

Refinement and concrete dependent values cannot contain co.const.none. An omitted initializer creates definitely-uninitialized storage; every read requires a valid assignment on all reachable paths or produces the compile-time diagnostic Uninitialized, and isNone() is invalid for those values.

The named diagnostic registry contains 66 stable case-sensitive Error-severity names covering the normative lexical, syntax, project, import, symbol, type, generic, overload, OOP, metadata, operator, effect, execution-model, usage, and backend rejection families.

Diagnostic names are reusable categories rather than declaration-specific sentences: DuplicateDeclaration covers non-callable symbol collisions, DuplicateCallableSignature covers normalized callable collisions, and OverloadNotAllowed covers categories that forbid overloading.
Metadata diagnostics distinguish unresolved form, invalid placement, invalid target, missing/invalid field, invalid value, and conflicting metadata so tooling can identify the failed compiler stage.

Every diagnostic instance carries severity, phase, message, primary span, optional related spans, and structured details. Implementations may add internal numeric identifiers but must preserve the registered public name.

Aggregate initialization is checked per construction path. Struct construction must establish all refinement/dependent fields before return or read; class @@new may yield co.lang.uninit, but each successful @@init overload must independently establish those fields before the instance becomes readable.
Equality, inequality, identity, ordering, and hashing involving none are unspecified. Backends may optimize the representation but may not expose raw host memory or backend undefined behavior.

continue supplies co.const.none for missing none-admitting call results and does not roll back prior side effects; return, return_with_error, and execution-model conversion follow the same restriction. A missing-result none substitution into a refinement or dependent position is invalid.

Closed co.lang.variants(...) results are recommended but not required for expected domain alternatives. A declared None-like constructor is an initialized variant value distinct from co.const.none, and continue does not manufacture it.

Every recoverable effect object is a class instance satisfying co.lang.error. The standard co.lang.AbstractError mixin supplies common state and concrete behavior and has composition semantics rather than class construction; custom error classes normally compose it while declaring co.lang.error, and explicit source mappings use co.dap.implement. co.dap.implementation remains reserved for backend-neutral runtime bindings such as co.runtime.operation.effect.emit.
Fatal failures do not satisfy co.lang.error and cannot enter effects metadata, handlers, or resolutions.

Every ExecutionModelFunctionDecl is a recoverable-effect boundary with exactly one co.lang.error-compatible result, no outward co.dap.effects contract, first-observed error conversion, and no effect propagation to the submitting caller.

co.dap.defer is error-independent completion registration: it injects no error or completion-status binding, captures only explicit parameters, and executes reached registrations in LIFO order on every enclosing-function exit.
@co.dap.oops now defines kind-checked ordered interfaces, classes, mixins, and traits fields; classes accepts at most two direct concrete parents.

this.classes[Type], this.mixins[Type], this.traits[Type], and this.interfaces[Type] are contextual compile-time selectors mapped directly to the matching @co.dap.oops fields. Keys use complete type names or import aliases and normalize to canonical declaration identity; numeric and computed keys are invalid.
this.parent selects the primary class parent, while this.parents[Type] aliases this.classes[Type]. The legacy this.base namespace and positional relationship access are absent.

Only classes[Type] participates in parent lifecycle lookup. mixins[Type] and traits[Type] may qualify composed implementation branches; interfaces[Type] produces an interface type/view and uses ordinary interface dispatch.

Class and mixin storage contributing to a class contains ordinary mutable per-instance fields only. Field-level constant, immutable, Shared, locking, and CopyOnWrite policies are rejected before inherited-state merging.
Accessible inherited class/mixin fields merge by identifier when canonical types match; broader accessibility wins and private fields are excluded from the child-visible merge.

co.lang.object requires ->(for=Target) or ->(for=[Class1, ...]) and denotes one independently named singleton. Annotation targets select annotation-implementation behavior; homogeneous non-empty class lists create explicit support associations.

A class-target object association is non-owning, non-structural, and non-transitive. It creates no companion owner or managed-reference graph edge and does not propagate inheritance, construction, copying, freezing, sharing, locking, CopyOnWrite behavior, or destruction.

Repeated canonical method declarations deduplicate. Distinct matching concrete methods within one relationship category use its first source; cross-category conflicts require explicit child resolution. Matching abstract and mandatory virtual slots may share one implementation or override.

FoLang has no abstract or unconstructable class category. Every co.lang.class has construction semantics; co.dap.sealed affects inheritance or overriding only. A co.lang.mixin is a separate composition declaration kind with no independent class-instance construction operation.
Trait validation now permits abstract/bodyless, default concrete, and valid virtual methods while continuing to forbid instance state.
